title: India Youth Uprising Tracker Update — Aug 31, 2026
summary: Two fresh institutional-trust flashpoints emerged beyond the exam-integrity fronts: Jamia Millia Islamia suspended and barred four NSUI-affiliated students on Aug 26 after a sit-in alleging spot-admission irregularities in the university's 2026-27 intake, which the administration denies. Separately, a student-and-alumni revolt over Chief Justice Surya Kant's planned attendance at law-school convocations — rooted in his handling of Jul 20 police-brutality petitions — forced NLSIU Bengaluru to cancel its Sep 12 convocation outright on Aug 27, after a similar Bar Council of India circular barring NALSAR Hyderabad's 2026 graduates from enrollment was retracted following backlash. No new developments were found on the CJP's planned September 5 return march since Delhi Police's Aug 26 refusal, or on the Jharkhand/Bihar exam-protest fronts since their Aug 17/Aug 27 concessions. Added 2 timeline events, 3 map points, 2 contested claims, 2 political profiles (Dhruv Chauhan, Manan Kumar Mishra) and 2 KPIs.

title: India Youth Uprising Tracker Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: The Delhi/CJP thread, dormant since the Jul 25 settlement, reawakens: the Cockroach Janta Party announced on Aug 24 that it will march again on September 5, from India Gate to Delhi Police headquarters, saying the government has kept only one of four settlement promises (Pradhan's resignation) while compensation for suicide victims' families, FIR withdrawals, and a police apology remain outstanding. Delhi Police confirmed on Aug 26 that no permission has been sought, cited standing prohibitory orders making an India Gate gathering illegal, and began staging paramilitary units, while CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka vowed the march would go ahead regardless. Added 2 timeline events, 2 map points (India Gate, Delhi Police HQ), 1 KPI, 1 contested claim, and 1 political profile (Ranka) covering this new escalation; the Jharkhand and Bihar exam-protest fronts remain unchanged since their Aug 17 and Aug 27 concessions.

title: India Youth Uprising Tracker Update — Aug 23, 2026
summary: A previously untracked parallel front in India's youth exam-integrity movement surfaces: a month-long protest in Ranchi, Jharkhand over alleged paper leaks and malpractice in JPSC/JSSC government recruitment exams. Job aspirants led by Devendra Nath Mahto began an open-ended sit-in on Jul 25, escalating through an Aug 10 march on the Assembly that police met with tear gas and water cannons, before the Jharkhand government cancelled the JSSC-CGL exam and all tests run by vendor TDPL since 2014 on Aug 17, forming a reforms committee and prompting Mahto to end his 16-day hunger strike. A planned Aug 20 siege of the Chief Minister's residence was called off, but the Jharkhand High Court has since stayed the exam cancellations for roughly 2,000 already-appointed candidates, leaving the protesters' central demand for a CBI probe unresolved. Added 7 timeline events, 4 map points, 2 casualty rows, 2 contested claims, 2 political profiles (Mahto, Hemant Soren) and 2 KPIs covering this new front.

title: India Youth Uprising Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: The NEET/CBSE-era street protests remain wound down since the July 25 settlement, but institutional friction over exam integrity resurfaced when the NTA's UGC-NET June 2026 papers were found riddled with errors. NSUI protesters clashed with Delhi Police and CRPF outside the NTA's Bhikaji Cama Place office on Aug 17, with several detained and NSUI reporting injuries among its members; the union's national president Vinod Jakhar demanded the NTA chairman's resignation. The NTA confirmed re-exams for English and Commerce on Sep 9 and Sociology on Sep 10, with no extra fee for candidates. Added a new casualty entry, a contested claim on the Aug 17 detentions, a map point for the NTA office protest site, and a new political profile for Jakhar.
